description: A property selector argument stands for the function that reads that property from each item
code:
orders = [{sku: "pen", qty: 2}, {sku: "ink", qty: 5}]
skus = orders.map(.sku)
units = orders.sum(.qty)
orders.push({sku: "cap", qty: 1})
[skus, units]

description: A dotted selector reads a nested path, and a missing step reads null
Selectors pass property reads to the population queries of a class
code:
class Bid(bidder, amount, open):
    this.bidder = bidder
    this.amount = amount
    this.open = open
leader = Bid.maxBy(.amount)
bidding = Bid.filter(.open).map(.bidder)
Bid("ada", 120, true)
Bid("bo", 150, false)
[leader.bidder, bidding, Bid.sum(.amount)]

description: A class-level rule that reads its lines with a selector stays live as lines are added
code:
class Order(lines): this.lines = lines
$Order.units = $Order.lines.sum(.qty)
order = Order([{qty: 2}])
order.lines.push({qty: 30})
order.units

description: A selector is an ordinary function argument of a user-defined function
A selector ignores extra arguments, so reduce reads the property of its accumulator
code:
chain = {at: 1, next: {at: 2, next: {at: 3, next: null}}}
steps = ["x", "y"]
hop = steps.reduce(.next, chain)
hop.at

description: Explanations render a selector argument as it is written
code:
class Bid(amount): this.amount = amount
Bid(40)
top = Bid.max(.amount)
(why top)[0].rule

description: Reading value through a selector whose argument is undefined raises a reference error naming the selector
code:
record = {}
failure = ""
try:
    [record.missing].map(.value)
catch error:
    failure = error
failure
